''[[Vuutun Palaa]]'', [[Naboo system]]{{BuildR2Cite|17|Droid Directory}} states that TC-14 was [[Death|destroyed]] when the [[Starship|ship]] she was aboard was destroyed at the culmination of the [[Battle of Naboo]]. ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles]]'' identifies this starship as the ''[[Vuutun Palaa]]'', which [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] depicts being destroyed in the [[Naboo system]]. |creator= |manufacturer=[[Cybot Galactica]]{{BuildR2Cite|17|Droid Directory}} |line= |model=[[TC-series protocol droid]] |class=[[Protocol droid]]{{Film|I}} |cost= |length= |width= |height=1.67 [[meter]]s (5[[Foot|ft]], 6in){{EncyclopediaCite|Protocol and Service Droids}} |mass= |gender=[[Gender|Feminine programming]]{{Databank|tc-14|TC-14}} |pronouns=She/her |sensor=[[Color|Yellow]] |plating=Silver |armament= |equipment=*Broadband [[antenna]] receiver *Logic functions [[computer]] *[[Microwave emitter/sensor]] |affiliation=[[Trade Federation]] }} {{Quote|I'm TC-14, at your service. This way please.|TC-14 greets the Jedi|audio=TC-14-Greeting.flac|}} '''TC-14''' was a [[Color|silver]]-plated [[TC-series protocol droid]] with [[Gender|feminine]] programming who was manufactured by [[Cybot Galactica]]. She served aboard the [[Trade Federation]] [[flagship]], ''[[Saak'ak]]'', where she frequently received [[memory wipe]]s that left her permanently confused and with no personality. In [[32 BBY]], she was aboard the ''Saak'ak'' when it was part of the Federation's [[blockade]] of the [[planet]] [[Naboo]]. The [[Protocol droid|droid]] greeted the [[Jedi]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] when they arrived aboard the [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter|vessel]] to negotiate an end to the blockade and reported that the visitors were Jedi to the [[Neimoidian]]s in charge of the [[starship]]. They sent her back to distract the Jedi and then attempted to [[assassin]]ate the pair while TC-14 was serving the Jedi drinks. The Jedi allowed TC-14 to leave unharmed, but she was later [[Death|destroyed]] during the [[Battle of Naboo]] after being transferred to the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk''-class Battleship]] ''[[Vuutun Palaa]]''. ==Biography== ===Greeting the Jedi=== {{Quote|What? What did you say?''"
"''The ambassadors are Jedi Knights, I believe.|Nute Gunray and TC-14|audio=Gunray-TC-14-JediKnights.flac|}} [[File:TC-14_distraction.png|thumb|right|300px|TC-14 was sent to distract the Jedi when they arrived aboard the ''Saak'ak''.]] Manufactured by [[Cybot Galactica]], TC-14 was a [[TC-series protocol droid]] with [[Gender|feminine programming]] who served the [[Trade Federation]] as the personal assistant of [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]]. Due to the paranoid nature of her masters, TC-14 had her memory wiped every two to three [[Standard week|weeks]] to prevent her from picking up vital Federation secrets to pass on to their competitors. During a trade dispute''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' in [[32 BBY]], she was stationed on board the Federation's [[flagship]], ''[[Saak'ak]]'', when the group [[blockade]]d the [[planet]] [[Naboo]] in the [[Naboo system]] under the orders of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]]. The [[Galactic Republic]] sent the [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to negotiate an end to the blockade, and after the Republic's [[Radiant VII|cruiser]] landed in one of the ''Saak'ak's'' [[hangar]]s, it was TC-14 who greeted the two [[Jedi]] at the hangar's entrance. She then led them to one of the [[Starship|flagship's]] conference rooms and left them upon arrival to report back to the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]]. On the bridge, she informed the [[viceroy]] and [[Captain]] [[Daultay Dofine]] as quickly as possible''[[Star Wars: Droidography]]'' that the [[ambassador]]s were Jedi, which horrified the [[Neimoidian]]s. Gunray ordered Dofine to distract the Jedi while he contacted Sidious, but the captain refused and ordered TC-14 to keep the ambassadors occupied instead. ===Disposable distraction=== {{Quote|Distract them, I will contact Lord Sidious.''"
"''Are you brain dead? I'm not going in there with two Jedi. Send the droid.|Nute Gunray and Daultay Dofine send TC-14 to distract the Jedi|audio=Gunray-Dofine-TC-14.flac|}} [[File:TC-14_and_battle_droids.png|thumb|left|300px|TC-14 was spared by the Jedi.]] TC-14 returned to the conference room with a tray of drinks for the two Jedi, who were growing restless. After they had both taken a cup from the tray, the pair leapt up and drew their [[lightsaber]]s, having sensed the [[Escape from the Saak'ak|destruction]] of their [[Consular-class light cruiser|cruiser]] in the hangar. TC-14 dropped the tray of drinks in shock and apologized as [[poison]]ous [[dioxis]] [[gas]] began pouring into the room through its vents. After some [[time]], Gunray—who had ordered the [[death]] of the Jedi after hearing from Sidious—sent a [[squad]] of [[OOM-series battle droid|battle droids]] to check if the pair had perished. They opened the door to the conference room, which had been sealed, and readied their [[blaster]]s; however, only TC-14 emerged, once again carrying the tray. The [[protocol droid]] quickly moved out of the squad's way and down a corridor, after which the two Jedi emerged from the gas and struck down the [[battle droid]]s. The Jedi ultimately escaped from the flagship and the Federation, which then [[Invasion of Naboo|invaded]] Naboo. TC-14's next scheduled memory wipe was brought forward in order to erase any evidence of the Neimoidian's attempts to kill the Jedi, but before it could take place, TC-14 was transferred along with Dofine to the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk''-class Battleship]] ''[[Vuutun Palaa]]'', where she was destroyed when the ship itself was destroyed by [[Anakin Skywalker]] at the culmination of the [[Battle of Naboo]]. The [[B1-series battle droid]] [[R0-GR]] later wrote about TC-14 in his ''[[Droidography]]'' [[book]], musing that if she had not followed her programming quite so precisely when dealing with the Jedi ambassadors, then the [[Clone Wars]] might never have occurred. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|Oh, sorry!|TC-14 apologizes as the Jedi sense danger|audio=TC-14-Sorry.flac|}} [[File:TC14crop-SWHC712.png|thumb|right|200px|TC-14 was a TC-series protocol droid who was left without a personality by constant memory wipes.]] TC-14's duties included carrying out the basic roles of a droid in her position, such as welcoming guests and serving refreshments. TC-14 received frequent [[memory wipe]]s from the Trade Federation, far beyond what was recommended for a droid, and as a result had no personality, conscience, or memory of any secrets she may have been privy to. The constant memory tampering also resulted in the droid having no life experience to compare to, meaning that she found everything slightly confusing and had a permanently baffled demeanor. As such, she found life aboard the Neimoidian vessels constantly bewildering as her owners began preparing for war, and she was confounded by the [[assassin]]ation attempted on the Jedi as she served them drinks. TC-14 was not programmed for duplicity and murder and so often found herself out of her depth working for the Trade Federation. Despite the protocol droid's programming, being caught in the crossfire between the battle droids and the Jedi produced levels of stress that TC-14 could not cope with. She also did not feel that aiding her masters in assassinating diplomatic visitors fell within her duties as a protocol droid, although, as she was endlessly polite, she did give her best efforts when keeping the Jedi busy and apologized to the battle droids while leaving the gas-filled conference room. TC-14's accessories included [[Audio sensor|auditory sensors]], a broadband [[antenna]] receiver, a logic functions [[computer]], a [[microwave emitter/sensor]], [[photoreceptor]]s, and a [[vocabulator]]. She had [[Color|silver]] plating, yellow photoreceptors, and stood 1.67 [[meter]]s (five [[Foot|feet]], six inches) tall. ==Behind the scenes== ===Film appearance=== {{Quote|What's quite nice is it isn't very robotic. It has, if I may say so, a very charming quality to it.|Lindsay Duncan, on TC-14's voice|{{InsiderCite|48|Voices of Episode I}}}} [[File:TC14_parts.jpg|thumb|left|250px|TC-14's costume was made from the same template as C-3PO and worn by John Fensom.]] TC-14 was physically portrayed by [[John Fensom]] and voiced by [[Lindsay Duncan]] in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which was released on [[May 19]], [[1999]].''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' Design director [[Doug Chiang]] drew concept art of TC-14 serving drinks to Obi-Wan Kenobi, finishing the piece on [[April 16]], [[1996]], after three days of work on it.''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]'' Casting director [[Robin Gurland]] offered Duncan the role after the actress auditioned for the role of [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]]. She was sent an artist's rendition of the character and then recorded her dialogue over a fairly short amount of time in a [[Wikipedia:London|London]] recording studio. Director [[George Lucas]] and Gurland were present for the recording and played a rough cut of the film for Duncan. She claimed that the film was the only work she had ever done that impressed her young son. TC-14 was built from the same costume template as [[C-3PO]].{{DB|droid|protocoldroid|protocol droid}} An alternate version of the scene where TC-14 greets the Jedi was animated and included two [[Wikipedia:Computer-generated imagery|computer generated]] droids discussing the arrival of the Republic cruiser, with [[PK-4/Legends|one]] stating that it must be important if Gunray sent a "useless protocol gearhead" to greet them.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' This scene was included in a revised fourth draft of the script dated to [[June 23]], [[1997]], which also uses the name "TC-3" for TC-14 and refers to the character with male pronouns.{{WebCite|url=https://usm.propstoreauction.com/m/lot-details/index/catalog/287/lot/74107|text=Lot # 1122: STAR WARS - EP I - THE PHANTOM MENACE (1999) - Revised Fourth Draft Script - Price Estimate: $800 - $1200|archivedate=20210625234234}} In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, TC-14 appeared prior to the release of ''The Phantom Menace'' in the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]], which was written by [[Terry Brooks]][[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]] and released on [[April 21]], 1999. ===LEGO=== {{Quote|Hello. Do you know who I am? Or what I am supposed to be doing? I appear to have no memory of my current identity or directive. Given the circumstance, I have ascertained that I am either a new model or have had my memory wiped. Any more information you can find would be invaluable.|TC-14 greets the player in ''LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga''|''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]''}} TC-14 appears in the [[2022]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' during an adaptation of her scene from the ''The Phantom Menace'' with slightly altered dialogue. The droid later appears in [[Theed]], the [[capital]] of Naboo, where she reveals to the player that she has lost her memory entirely and asks them to investigate what happened in the quest "Mysterious Endeavor." If the player refuses, she is understanding, but realizes that the answers she seeks are unlikely to reveal themselves on their own. Once the player accepts, TC-14 notices a masked [[Unidentified enigmatic Neimoidian|Neimoidian]] watching nearby and asks the player to locate him after he flees. After questioning several citizens, the player locates the hiding Neimoidian and then chases him down when he once again tries to run. Once the Neimoidian is caught, TC-14 joins the player as the Neimoidian explains that he served with TC-14 onboard the ''Vuutun Palaa'', but when the ship's destruction looked imminent he decided to escape. TC-14 refused to abandon her duties and join him in deserting, so he deactivated her and [[Smuggler|smuggled]] her into Theed before wiping her memory so that she would not remember that he had forced her to desert. TC-14 then reveals that she has heard the Neimoidian's confession, and after he apologizes and claims he planned to tell her the truth at some point, she forgives him, as if he had not smuggled her off the ship she would have perished and been unable to perform her duties anyway. The Neimoidian then describes his actions as heroic, but TC-14 disagrees. With the mystery solved, the droid then also thanks the player, offering to enter their service since she no longer has any duties. This completes the quest and unlocks TC-14 as a purchasable character costing 35,000 studs. Later, in the Trade Federation hideout in Theed, the Neimoidian laments TC-14's departure: he had planned to ask her to stay as a helper droid; instead, he has to do his own dishes and scrub his own floors, left to wish that he had remained on the ''Vuutun Palaa''. ==Appearances== *{{Film|I}} {{1st}} *''[[Star Wars Epic Adventures: The Phantom Menace]]'' *[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace Graphic Novel Adaptation|''Star Wars: The Phantom Menace'' Graphic Novel Adaptation]] *''[[Star Wars: The Prequel Trilogy – A Graphic Novel]]'' *{{StoryCite|story=Short Negotiations (5-Minute Star Wars Stories Strike Back)|book=5-Minute Star Wars Stories Strike Back|audiobook=1}} ===Non-canon appearances=== *''[[William Shakespeare's The Phantom of Menace: Star Wars Part the First]]'' *{{LegoMiniMovie|series=Stop-Motion Story|text=The One With The Giant Space Slug|video=NNzswgjKbuM}} *''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' ==Sources== *''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' *''[[Ultimate Factivity Collection: Star Wars]]'' {{Po}} *{{HelmetCollectionCite|3|Weapons & Uniforms}} *[[Star Wars: What is a Wookiee?
